detailed_description: The Team Generator tool employs a hybrid randomization and optimization algorithm to partition individuals into balanced teams based on customizable metrics. This tool addresses the inherent challenges of equitable group distribution in scenarios requiring skill balance, size constraints, or diversity considerations. Using a combination of Fisher-Yates shuffling for initial randomization and a constraint satisfaction algorithm for post-processing adjustments, the system dynamically evaluates participant attributes like skill ratings, experience levels, or physical attributes to minimize inter-team variance. The backend implements a weighted graph partitioning approach when skill metrics are provided, ensuring balanced distribution of high/medium/low performers across teams. For unquantified groups, it defaults to round-robin name allocation after cryptographic randomization using a 256-bit entropy source. Technical features include adjustable team size caps, forced member pairing/avoidance through constraint flags, and CSV import/export capabilities with UTF-8 encoding support. The tool's value proposition lies in eliminating manual bias in team creation while maintaining computational efficiency - handling 100-person groups in <200ms through optimized quicksort implementations.
usage_steps: 1. Input Participant Data: Paste newline-separated names into the 'Participants' text area (supports 2-100 entries)
2. Define Attributes: Use the 'Skill Level' dropdown to assign metrics (Low/Medium/High) for each participant
3. Configure Constraints: Toggle 'Avoid Conflicts' to activate pairing restrictions via the conflict matrix
4. Set Parameters: Adjust 'Teams' numeric input and enable 'Balanced Sizes' for strict equal team distribution
5. Initialize Randomization: Choose entropy source (Browser CryptoAPI or Custom Seed) in the 'Randomization' section
6. Execute & Export: Click 'Generate Teams' and download results as CSV or JSON with attribute preservation
usage_examples: Example 1: Esports tournament organizers balancing 32 competitive players into 8 ranked teams using MMR (Matchmaking Rating) data imported via CSV
Example 2: Corporate HR team creating 5 cross-functional project groups with enforced departmental diversity constraints
Example 3: Physical education instructor assigning 24 students to 4 sports teams with balanced gender and skill level distribution
Example 4: Academic research coordinator forming 6 thesis groups with required pairing of senior/junior students and equipment sharing constraints
